title: Experiment Orchestration Broker Pattern - Notes (wip)
body:
Goal: sketch the broker pattern for cross-team experiment orchestration that decouples routing, safety gates, and telemetry collection.

Context (why this doc):
- We have many ad-hoc experiment flows: feature flags + client-side splitters, console A/B via the routing layer, ad-hoc canaries done by infra teams.
- Pain points: duplicated routing logic, inconsistent guardrails across teams, difficulty enforcing cost/latency budgets for LLM-backed endpoints, telemetry fragmentation.
- Proposed: an "Experiment Broker" that sits between the Console/FF system and serving runtime. It centralizes slice allocation, enforces risk policies, emits canonical telemetry, and exposes a small API for product owners and SREs.

High-level responsibilities for the Experiment Broker:
1) Allocation: accept requests to register experiments (cohorts, weights, exclusion rules) and return deterministic route decisions.
2) Guardrails: apply safety policies (latency budget, cost cap, safety-tier gating) and optionally short-circuit to fallback models/paths.
3) Observability: emit standardized event stream (experiment_id, cohort_id, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_consumed, error_type, inference_result_hash) to our telemetry pipeline.
4) Rollout controls: support manual pause, auto-threshold pause (based on telemetry), rollback API.
5) Quotas: enforce per-experiment throughput caps to protect capacity for tiered customers.

Consumer surface (API sketch):
- POST /experiments - register experiment: {id, cohorts:[{name,weight}], model_map, safety_profile}
- GET /route?user_id=...&request_id=... - returns {experiment_id, cohort, model_variant, fallback_reason?}
- POST /signal - manual override/traffic shift (for on-call)
- Webhook notifications for pause/rollback events

Operational flows (examples):
- Product creates experiment in Console -> Broker validates (no overlap, capacity check) -> Broker returns experiment id -> SDK/edge calls GET /route for each request -> Serving runtime honors model_variant.
- Canary: create tiny cohort (0.5% traffic) with strict safety_profile (latency_budget: 200ms, sentiment_degradation_threshold: -0.05). If broker receives pause signal from telemetry, switch cohort to fallback model.

Safety_profile ideas (configurable on register):
- latency_budget_ms (per-route): numeric
- token_cost_limit_per_minute: numeric
- behavioral_checks: list (e.g., profanity_rate_threshold, hallucination_score_delta)
- fallback_policy: {immediate_fallback: boolean, gradual_shift: {step_pct:5,step_window_minutes:10}}

Telemetry & Signals (minimal canonical list):
- request_id, experiment_id, cohort, model_variant, region, latency_ms, inference_tokens, client_route_version
- outcome signals: error_rate_5m, p95_latency, median_tokens, negative_sentiment_rate
- derived safety signals: drift_score (compared to baseline prompt set), content-violation-rate

Escalation & auto-pause logic (initial proposal):
- If p95_latency > baseline_p95 * 1.25 for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> pause cohort
- If error_rate_5m > baseline_error_rate + 0.02 -> notify and start 2x sampling to debug
- If negative_sentiment_rate increased by > 0.1 absolute on control vs experiment -> pause and require human review

Checklist for experiment registration (product owner / console):
- [ ] hypothesis & primary/secondary metrics documented (Confluence link)
- [ ] experiment_id reserved and mapped to ticket (Jira key)
- [ ] safety_profile chosen, fallback policy defined
- [ ] rollout cadence: initial pct, ramp plan, stop conditions
- [ ] linked evals/prompt-set included
- [ ] contacts: owner, oncall, data-analyst

Operator playbook (oncall):
- On alert: check broker event stream for experiment_id
- If auto-pause occurred: inspect p95 latency and error types, compare to baseline (last 24h)
- If manual rollback needed: fire POST /signal with rollback command and notify stakeholders (Slack + PagerDuty)
- Post-mortem: capture root cause, whether model or infra. Tag experiment as "failed" or "needs follow-up" in Console.

Design considerations / tradeoffs:
- Deterministic routing vs latency: synchronous GET /route adds a hop. Options: client-side SDK with cached decisions (TTL) or piggyback routing in edge proxy. Optimize for low-latency paths by pre-fetching decisions for session-based flows.
- Centralized broker simplifies policy enforcement but is a single point to scale/secure. We'll need sharded brokers and local-cache layer.
- Safety checks cost compute: prefer lightweight heuristics in real-time and heavier batch evals offline.

Questions & unresolved items (notes-to-self):
- How do we represent hierarchical experiments (experiment A contains sub-experiments)?
- Mapping to Dedicated customers: should their reserved capacity be exempt from experiment throttles? or have separate quota profiles?
- Legal/compliance: for Private deployments, broker must be available in-customer VPC or replaced by a local equivalent. Need to scope for Private offering.
- Data residency: telemetry from Private deployments may not flow to central telemetry; broker should support local sinks and a summary telemetry callback.

Action items (owners assigned):
- Ethan: prototype GET /route shim in edge proxy (due 2024-10-09)
- Sofia: draft broker schema + safety_profile proto and post to Confluence (due 2024-09-20)
- Liam: run load simulation (10k rps patterns with experiment lookups) and report latency impact (due 2024-09-27)
- Priya: map required telemetry fields to our existing pings and Nanny dashboards; propose new visualizations (due 2024-10-03)

Quick simulation notes (scratch):
- If we add 1 synchronous lookup at 1ms median with 1ms variance, 99th at 5ms, edge added latency acceptable for most flows but not for ultra-low-latency routes. Consider TTL=30s cached route decisions keyed by user-session.
- For cohort-size calculation: sampling 0.5% on 1M DAU -> 5k qps; must ensure fallback capacity or cost caps.

Appendix: sample slack templates (for oncall comms)
- "Experiment <id> auto-paused by broker due to p95 latency breach. Immediate action: investigate scaling or fallback. Links: <console link> <broker event link>"
- "Manual rollback for <id> initiated by <owner>. Notifying infra and data teams. Case: <short reason>"

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, link to the canonical schema page once Sofia shares it. We should avoid duplicating the Console's experiment model; broker should reference Console ids.
